full.message: WebMCP tools were detected and reviewed.
full.summary: This is a strong, coherent WebMCP surface with a consistent result envelope, precise input/output schemas, and unusually careful guidance around cost-avoidance, confirmation flows, and security-sensitive tokens. The booking lifecycle (options → availability → start → cancel) is well-sequenced with explicit two-step confirmation and clear UTC/timezone handling. It falls short of a 5 mainly due to all tools living on a single page (thin page coverage) and some intent overlap between the concierge and the factual lookup tools that relies on prose disambiguation rather than structural separation.
highlights: Consistent ok/error envelope across all tools
All tools on one page — thin coverage

perToolNotes.note: Clear, but broad catch-all; overlap with lookups managed only via description.

perToolNotes.name: list_offerings

perToolNotes.name: get_pricing
perToolNotes.note: Authoritative and detailed; plan enum and fields well defined.

perToolNotes.name: recommend_plan
perToolNotes.note: Deterministic with sensible bounded inputs; reasons/caveats aid transparency.

perToolNotes.name: get_setup_instructions
perToolNotes.note: Returns concrete steps/snippet; optional narrowing param is clear.

perToolNotes.name: list_customer_examples
perToolNotes.note: Useful proof tool; simple bounded limit param.

perToolNotes.name: get_booking_options
perToolNotes.note: Good precondition sequencing and timezone semantics; solid enums.

perToolNotes.name: check_availability
perToolNotes.note: Excellent range constraints, empty-list semantics, and UTC vs local handling.

perToolNotes.name: start_booking
perToolNotes.note: Exemplary two-step commit with strong anti-hallucination and cancel_url secrecy notes.

perToolNotes.name: cancel_booking
perToolNotes.note: Careful token-only auth, idempotency, and null-time-before-confirm handling.

tools.name: ask_concierge
tools.description: Ask this business's concierge a question in natural language — hours, policies, recommendations, anything a guest would ask at the desk. Replies come from the same knowledge and conversation engine the human-facing chat on this page uses, and context is kept across calls so follow-ups work. Use this for judgement and nuance. Do NOT use it for facts the free lookup tools already return — prefer get_business_info for contact details and list_offerings for services, which are instant and cost nothing. Returns { ok, answer, conversation_id }.

question.description: The visitor's question, in natural language. One question per call; the concierge answers conversationally.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this reply belongs to. Stable across calls on this page.

tools.name: get_business_info
tools.description: Verified public facts about this business: name, how it introduces itself, published contact details, the topics it invites questions about, and whether it can take a booking. Free and instant, no conversation started. Call this FIRST for anything factual — it is cheaper and more reliable than asking the concierge. Returns { ok, name, introduction, contact { email, phone, url }, suggested_topics[], booking_available }. Every Lobby tool returns that same envelope: `ok`, plus `error` with `code` and `message` when `ok` is false, alongside its own payload.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

introduction.description: How the business introduces itself to a visitor.

contact.description: Published contact details, or null if none.

suggested_topics.description: Topics this concierge is prepared to discuss.

booking_available.description: True when this concierge exposes booking tools. When false, nothing here can be scheduled — offer the contact details instead of implying a booking is possible.

tools.name: list_offerings
tools.description: The services this business offers, as structured data an agent can compare, filter or present. Each offering carries an explicit `bookable` flag — check it before attempting to schedule anything. Free and instant. Returns { ok, offerings[] of { id, name, description, price, currency, bookable, action_url, contact_required }, total, booking_available }.

bookable_only.description: When true, return only offerings that can be scheduled through the booking tools. Default false (return all).

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

offerings.description: The business’s services, comparable and filterable.

id.description: Stable id to pass to other tools.

price.description: Null when the business does not publish a price.

bookable.description: True only when this specific offering can be scheduled through the booking tools. Never assume a bookable offering from the presence of a booking tool.

contact_required.description: True when arranging this offering needs a human — use the contact details from get_business_info.

booking_available.description: Whether this concierge can book at all. False means every offering is contact-only regardless of its own flag.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Lobby's plans: prices, monthly conversation allowances, what each tier includes, and what happens on going over. Authoritative and free — use this rather than reading prices off the page, and rather than asking the concierge. Returns { ok, currency, plans[] of { id, name, price_monthly, price_annual, monthly_conversations, shows_lobby_badge, includes_booking, features[], signup_url }, overage, what_counts_as_a_conversation }.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

includes_booking.description: Whether concierges on this plan can take bookings.

tools.name: recommend_plan
tools.description: Which Lobby plan fits a described business, and why. Deterministic — it compares the stated needs against the published allowances and features, it does not guess. Prefer this over asking the concierge "which plan should I pick", which cannot see the numbers. Returns { ok, recommended_plan_id, recommended_plan_name, price_monthly, reasons[], caveats[], signup_url }.

expected_monthly_conversations.description: Roughly how many visitor sessions a month. One visitor session is one conversation however many messages it holds.

number_of_sites.description: How many websites need a concierge.

needs_own_branding.description: True when the business wants the "Built with Lobby" footer gone.

needs_booking.description: True when visitors should be able to book an appointment through the concierge.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

reasons.description: Why this plan, in order of weight.

caveats.description: Things the visitor should know before committing. May be empty.

tools.name: get_setup_instructions
tools.description: How a business puts Lobby on its website: the one-line embed script for an existing site, or the hosted concierge page for a business without one. Returns { ok, options[] of { id, name, when_to_use, steps[], snippet }, signup_url } — the actual steps and the snippet shape, not a summary of them.

has_existing_website.description: True narrows the answer to the embed route, false to the hosted page. Omit for both.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

tools.name: list_customer_examples
tools.description: Live Lobby concierges an agent or a person can actually visit and try. Real published pages, not testimonials. Use these as proof when a visitor asks "who is using this" or "show me one working". Returns { ok, examples[] of { slug, url, agent_tools_available }, total }.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

agent_tools_available.description: Every hosted concierge page registers WebMCP tools, so an agent can visit and use it directly.

tools.name: open_signup
tools.description: The URL to start a Lobby account, and optionally navigate there. Signup is free and needs only an email address — no card. This is not a committing action, but it does move the visitor off the current page when `navigate` is true, so prefer returning the URL and letting them click unless they asked to be taken there. Returns { ok, url, navigated, requirements[] }.

plan.description: Which plan to start on. Default free.

navigate.description: When true, navigate this page to signup. Default false — navigating away ends the current conversation.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

requirements.description: What the visitor needs in order to sign up.

tools.name: get_booking_options
tools.description: What can be booked with this business, and for how long. Returns the bookable appointment types with their durations. Call this before check_availability — availability is always relative to one booking type, because duration determines which slots fit. Returns { ok, booking_types[] of { id, name, description, duration_minutes, price, currency, location_kind }, timezone }.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

timezone.description: IANA zone the business keeps its hours in. Slot times are returned as absolute UTC instants regardless, so a visitor in another zone is never offered a time that does not exist.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Free times for one booking type in a date range. Every slot is a real opening: the business’s published hours minus anything already on its calendar. An empty list is a definite "nothing free in that range", not an error — widen the range or offer to take a message. Returns { ok, slots[] of { start_utc, end_utc, start_local }, total, timezone, searched { from_date, to_date } }.

to_date.description: Last date to consider, YYYY-MM-DD, INCLUSIVE. Omit for a single day. At most 60 days after from_date.

visitor_timezone.description: The visitor's IANA timezone, if known (e.g. 'Europe/Berlin'). Slot times are echoed in it for display. Omit and the business’s own zone is used.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

start_local.description: Same instant, formatted in visitor_timezone, for showing a person. Never pass this back — pass start_utc.

tools.name: start_booking
tools.description: Book one of the free slots from check_availability. THIS COMMITS the visitor to an appointment and emails the business, so it is deliberately two-step: call it first WITHOUT `confirmed`, show the returned summary to the visitor in their own words, and only call it again with `confirmed: true` once they have explicitly agreed. Never set `confirmed: true` on the first call, and never infer agreement from the visitor merely having asked about times. Returns { ok, status, summary { what, when_utc, duration_minutes, guest_name, guest_email, business }, booking_id }. The visitor is emailed a confirmation with a calendar invitation attached and their own cancellation link. `cancel_url` is null here and stays null on purpose: that link is the visitor’s only credential for their appointment and it is not handed to a tool caller. If the visitor later wants to cancel, ask them for the token in that email and use cancel_booking — do not send them to the business, and do not try their booking_id.

start_utc.description: Exactly as returned by check_availability. Do not construct or round this yourself.

guest_name.description: The name the visitor gave you, as they gave it. This is what the business will see on the appointment.

guest_email.description: Where the confirmation goes. Ask the visitor; never invent, guess or reuse an address from elsewhere on the page.

notes.description: Anything the business should know beforehand.

confirmed.description: The visitor has seen the summary and explicitly agreed. Omit or false on the first call.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

status.description: `needs_confirmation` means NOTHING was booked yet. `booked` means the appointment exists, is on the business’s calendar, and a confirmation email has gone to the address given — carrying a calendar invitation and the visitor’s own cancellation link. Tell them to expect it. The appointment itself does not depend on that email: `booked` is the record, and a mail delay is not a booking that failed.

summary.description: Exactly what will be, or has been, booked. Read this back to the visitor verbatim before confirming.

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description: Cancel an appointment the visitor already has, using the cancellation token from their own confirmation email. THIS RELEASES the slot, tells the business, and cannot be undone, so it is two-step exactly like start_booking: call it first WITHOUT `confirmed`, read the returned summary back to the visitor, and only call it again with `confirmed: true` once they have explicitly agreed. Ask the visitor for the cancellation link or token from their confirmation email — that token is the ONLY thing that authorises this, and a booking id will not work and must not be tried. Never guess, construct, or reuse a token, and never take one from anywhere but the visitor you are speaking to. Returns { ok, status, summary { business, cancels, when_utc } }.

cancel_token.description: The token from the visitor’s confirmation email — either the token itself or the last path segment before /cancel in their cancellation link. This is a secret belonging to that one appointment. It is NOT the booking_id that start_booking returns, and passing an id here is refused.

confirmed.description: The visitor has seen the summary and explicitly agreed to cancel. Omit or false on the first call.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

status.description: `needs_confirmation` means NOTHING was cancelled yet and the appointment still stands. `cancelled` means the slot is free again, the calendar entry is gone, and both the visitor and the business have been emailed. Cancelling twice is safe and reports `cancelled` both times — the backend is idempotent, so a repeated call is never an error and never a second cancellation.

summary.description: What will be, or has been, cancelled. Read this back to the visitor before confirming.

cancels.description: Plain-language description of the appointment the token belongs to, for reading aloud.

when_utc.description: When the cancelled appointment was to start, as the backend reports it. NULL before confirmation: nothing previews a booking by token, so the time is genuinely not known until the cancellation is made. Do not invent a time for the visitor on the first call — ask them to confirm from their own email instead.

suggestedJourneys.text: I want to add Lobby's concierge to my existing website—retrieve the exact embed script steps and give me the free-plan signup URL.
Check whether this business has any bookable appointment types, and if so, find the earliest free slot in October 2026 for the shortest one.
Ask the concierge if Lobby can handle multiple languages, then get the setup instructions for a business that does not have a website yet.
